Alocución del Director General a la 
58ª Asamblea Mundial de la Salud 
Ginebra, lunes 16 de mayo de 2005 
El Director General empieza hablando en francés. 
Señor Presidente de la República de Maldivas, señor Bill Gates, señora Presidenta, honorables mi-
nistros, distinguidos delegados, señoras y señores: 
1. 
Hace 60 años los dirigentes mundiales protagonizaron un intenso debate sobre la manera de garanti-
zar el bienestar de la humanidad después de la Segunda Guerra Mundia

summary.text: Opens the Spanish text of the WHO Director-General's address to the 58th World Health Assembly in May 2005, recalling the founding of the UN system 60 years earlier and thanking the Vienna Philharmonic as a new goodwill ambassador. It notes that, despite progress, child mortality reduction targets are at risk of being missed.

summary.text: Continues the Director-General's 2005 address, observing that health indicators have not improved as hoped even though coverage of some interventions has risen. It welcomes increased funding for health development and introduces the 2006–2007 programme budget, with increases for epidemic response, maternal and child health, noncommunicable diseases, tobacco control and emergencies. It cites the use of WHO's coordination capacity after the Asian tsunami and during the Marburg outbreak in Angola.

summary.text: Continues the address with lessons from the tsunami response, where WHO warnings and quick action on water, nutrition and surveillance helped prevent further harm. It argues that action without knowledge is as useless as knowledge without action. It stresses coordination, clear communication and shared understanding in disease control.

summary.text: Continues the address, citing the Marburg response in Angola, where villagers feared health workers, as showing the need for understanding of health measures. It highlights research, an international clinical trials registry and the new Commission on Social Determinants of Health, and calls for solidarity among partners.

summary.text: Continues the address with WHO's aim of universal access to care through partnership against infectious and chronic diseases. It cites progress in the drive to treat three million people with HIV/AIDS by the end of 2005 and the role of the WHO prequalification project. It also previews the coming World Health Report on human resources for health.

También se encuentran bien avanzados los preparativos del Programa General de Trabajo pa-
ra 2006-2015, que se presentará a la Asamblea de la Salud el año próximo.  Tratará del modo de fomentar 
el bienestar humano a través del acceso a la asistencia, el control de las epidemias y el mejoramiento de la 
calidad de vida.  La distribución de las enfermedades cambia, pero está claro que hoy y mañana, como 
cuando se redactó la Constitución de la OMS, la salud es básica «para la felicidad, las relaciones armonio-
sas y la seguridad de todos los pueblos».

summary.text: Concludes the Director-General's 2005 address, previewing the General Programme of Work for 2006–2015 and discussing the return of polio to Yemen and Indonesia alongside gains in Nigeria, India and Pakistan. It names the funding gap as the main threat to eradication and closes with a call to put knowledge into action.
